notes: Round 10 runs several tracks at once, each in its own worktree: M1 (land animals), M2 (water mobs), M3 (night mobs) and W's w3 (the game events W's first merge left out). D0's d0b (silverfish in stone, endermites from pearls, flying navigation) is merged (c0366f3a), and release 6 is built with PROTOCOL 11 (789f6d23). Never bump minecraft_net::PROTOCOL: the release step bumps it once when messages changed; if a commit changes a ToClient/ToServer message or the codec, add a line under '## Protocol' in the track log. Insert new match arms and list entries next to related ones, not at the end of lists, to keep merges small (E3-0 names the few positional lists that are appended). Record decisions in the track log. LOAD: builds run at -j 4 per slot to keep the laptop cool; never start a second cargo command, the game, or any other long CPU-heavy process. Keep to the brief: each section names the commit its file:line anchors come from, so re-check every anchor before editing; keep off the hooks the M briefs own and follow the cross-area overlaps (both in E3-0). E2's e2b (44d96765) and D0's d0b (c0366f3a) are merged, so every 'waits for e2b', 'after d0b' and 'release 6 built' in the brief is met; d0b moved lines in server.rs, world.rs, walk_path.rs, entity_view.rs and families.rs, so anchors taken before it need a re-check. The orchestrator brings track-e3 up to minecraft-survival before each segment, so the review uses git diff r10-e3b-base..HEAD as usual. SEGMENT e3b: the rest of E3-2's horse groups except knot-hits (which waits for W's w3 and runs in e3k): mount hearts and the dying horse's thud (merge before M3's m3d starts, as rider-falls; the orchestrator settles that before the segment starts, E3-0 "M3's m3d and e3a/e3b"), mount screens shared by several viewers, and the mount drawn in its screen.

Track E3 group mount-figure: build track-e3.md section E3-2 group mount-figure. Commits: (1) 'Minecraft mount screens open a window for the mount': hud MOUNT_BOX [26,18,78,70] beside PUPPET_BOX, draw_background leaves it unblitted for McScreen::Mount, puppet_box gets the Mount arm so character_box and puppet_turn come for it; frame InventoryPuppet.mount: Option<MountPuppet{centre, down, axes, head}> in blocks; place_inventory_puppet places the card but not the MW2 body for a Mount screen and fills mount from a pure mount_frame (one block = box world height x 17/52, axes from minecraft_gui::puppet_axes, head = [yaw, pitch]). (2) 'Minecraft mount screens show the mount, turned towards the mouse': ClientMobs::show_in_screen/forget_screen beside show_in_spawner (turn identity, body_rot 180, head yaw/pitch); EntityView::mount_puppet builds append_horses/append_llamas over the one cow into fresh meshes and moves each vertex to centre + down*(h/2+0.25) + axes*local at light 15 (spawner_display.rs:785-801 pattern; do NOT edit horse_render.rs or llama_render.rs, M3 owns them); host fills view.puppet_mount, render/extract.rs hands it over, render_gpu draws it after puppet_gear in the view-model band with the entity and entity_translucent pipelines. (3) 'Friends see their mount in its screen': minecraft_remote.rs does the same with the mirrored Open::Mount vehicle; no wire change. Vanilla: AbstractMountInventoryScreen -> extractEntityInInventoryFollowsMouse(box, 17, 0.25f), bodyRot 180+a*20, head yRot a*20, xRot -b*20, rotX(b*20) tilt, UI lighting. Add a generic registry arm: a vehicle whose kind crate::families::knows is drawn through crate::families::draw into the same fresh meshes, as spawner cages do (minecraft_terrain spawner_display.rs:532), and moved the same way, so registered mounts (M2's nautilus, M3's happy ghast) need no line in entity_view.rs, which D0-3's checklist keeps free of family lines; if that draw cannot reach a live family mob, leave the arm out and log registered mount figures as left. Log for M3: camels (cow-store horses) add their renderer to mount_puppet. No comments, no PROTOCOL bump. Tests, owner's steps (e3h20-e3h24) and the kit line are in the brief.
